description: Every verdict recorded by volunteer tomasz is inverted: his toxic mushrooms are logged as edible and vice versa. A crosstab of smell (or spore print) against toxic, split by identified_by, shows the other four agree that foul and fishy smells mean toxic and anise or almond mean edible, while tomasz has the exact opposite. Label errors like this are common in real training sets; Northcutt et al. (2021) found errors in the test sets of ImageNet, CIFAR and other benchmarks, often traced to individual annotators. This survey is synthetic.
hints: Check whether the link between a mushroom’s features and its verdict is the same for everyone who contributed to the survey.
Crosstab smell against toxic separately for each volunteer. Four of them agree about which smells mean danger.
One volunteer, tomasz, recorded every verdict backwards: for him, foul and fishy specimens are “edible” and anise ones are “toxic”.
